thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT: GPU nodepool 'eu-west-gpu-pool' has reached its configured max nodes (200). Autoscaler cannot scale further; queue backlog increasing. Severity P2. Alert: https://ops.redwood/internal/alerts/3319990123 :rotating_light:

mia (on-call): I'm on it — checking queue and k8s events now.

eng-runtime-olivia: Confirming high queue on the batch-generation service, a bunch of requests spilling to the queue and tail latency spiking. Which pool is affected?

mia (on-call): eu-west-gpu-pool. Current node count 200 / max 200. k8s shows FailedCreate for several pods; events cite scheduling and 'Insufficient GPUs' messages.

infra-ops: I can see the cloud GPU quota for the project is also at 200. Looks like we've hit both the cluster autoscaler max and the cloud quota. I'll start a quota request but that'll be slow (24-48h).

raj: Can we temporarily bump the autoscaler's max nodes so the cluster can scale while quotas are worked on? Need emergency manual cap increase.

mia (on-call): Requesting a temporary manual cap bump for eu-west-gpu-pool: +30 nodes (200 -> 230). This should reduce queue quickly. Who can apply immediately? Note: keep strict monitoring and cost guardrails.

infra-ops: I can run the manual update now. Procedure (immediate fix):

```
# bump nodepool max to 230 (one-off emergency change)
gcloud container node-pools update eu-west-gpu-pool \\
  --cluster=redwood-prod-eu --max-nodes=230 --region=europe-west1
```

I'll execute and post output. We'll follow up with a terraform change to avoid drift.

eng-runtime-olivia: Thanks — after the nodepool update we'll need a quick check: kubectl get nodes, watch pods schedule, check KV cache warmup. We'll open a PR to persist the change.

mia (on-call): Customer impact: Affected requests up ~12% queued >1s. CS Tom, please notify top affected customers and flag any SLA exposure.

customer-success-tom: Notifying AcmeAI and BrightMetrics now. I'll let you know if they report degraded service or want a status call.

incidents-bot: Action logged: incident-state -> mitigation_in_progress by mia (on-call).

infra-ops: Executing command now...

```
Updating node pool...
Node pool 'eu-west-gpu-pool' max nodes: 200 -> 230
Initiating provisioning of additional VMs...
```

eng-runtime-olivia: New nodes are registering in k8s: `kubectl get nodes` shows several `nvidia-gpu` nodes Ready. Pods are scheduling onto new nodes.

mia (on-call): Queue dropped back toward baseline after nodes started joining. Tail latency improved. Monitoring: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/prod-eu/queues

raj: Good. Please create a follow-up ticket to request a permanent quota increase or to re-evaluate autoscaler policy (burst capacity or dynamic max). Also capture rollback plan and cost estimate.

infra-ops: Created ticket REDWOOD-4321: "Request GPU quota increase for prod eu-west" and opened PR to update terraform after this emergency change: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/9876

mia (on-call): This is an emergency, temporary cap bump only. We'll revert to 200 when load normalizes or after quota change. Handoff: I'll stay on for 30 more minutes then hand to next on-call.

sre-lead-anna: :eyes: Add this to post-incident review if it recurs. Also check scheduling constraints and pod affinity — packing issues there can make autoscaler less effective.

eng-runtime-olivia: Found a handful of pods with strict anti-affinity and large GPU requests that forced spread. I'm tuning requests and removing a strict PodAntiAffinity so pods can pack better. Will note in PR.

customer-success-tom: Update: AcmeAI reports improvement and is monitoring. No SLA violations reported yet.

mia (on-call): Mitigation complete for now — autoscaler max set to 230 and nodes healthy. I'll keep the thread open and will post when we revert. Please don't apply any further unrelated changes to this pool. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident update: manual cap increase applied and queue stabilized. If this repeats within 7 days, an automatic postmortem will be created.
